classification.difficultyReason: Complete cubic factorisation supports a deduction about divisibility for every integer input.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $P(2)=0$ and hence, fully factorise $P(x)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(2)&=2^3-9(2)^2+26(2)-24\\P(2)&=8-36+52-24\\P(2)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Hence, $x-2$ is a factor. Long division by $x-2$ gives the quotient $x^2-7x+12$.
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-2)(x^2-7x+12)\\P(x)&=(x-2)(x-3)(x-4).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Deduce that $P(x)$ will always output multiples of six for any integer value of $x$.

answer.short: For integer $x$, $(x-2)(x-3)(x-4)$ is a product of three consecutive integers. It contains an even integer and a multiple of $3$, so $P(x)$ is divisible by $6$.
answer.worked: For integer $x$, the factors $x-4$, $x-3$ and $x-2$ are three consecutive integers. At least one is even, and one is divisible by $3$. Their product is therefore divisible by $2\times3=6$.
